blocks.source: Vol III, Introduction, § Reliability and Cost over a Horizon
blocks.md: A realistic agentic trajectory spans dozens of sequential turns, with each turn building directly on observations and state modifications from the preceding step. In the repair task, a misdiagnosed deadlock trace from the failing test leads the model to inspect the wrong source file; an erroneous patch to that file cascades into compilation failures or silently corrupts unrelated business logic. Because foundation models generate fluent rationalizations even when mistaken, nothing in the model's generated text signals the exact moment execution derailed.

questions.q: The section **Reliability and Cost over a Horizon** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A trajectory that waits on a tool must decouple task lifetime from the serving allocation, or retained state occupies scarce memory while no tokens are produced.
Under retry-until-accept, C_eff = E[C_attempt]/p_acc, so acceptance divides the whole attempt cost and any mechanism pays for its overhead only if it lowers this ratio.
The characteristic agent failure is well-formed, credible, and wrong, so fail-stop monitors record success and agreement among samples from one model sets no bound on wrong answers.

Self-report, static analysis, visible tests, sealed tests, and formal verification form a default ordering of acceptance evidence that coverage can override, and every check is a bounded claim narrower than the task.
